items.heading: Fresher Hiring in India Does
items.text: Fresher hiring in India does not use one universal format, but a common shape shows up across most campus drives and off-campus fresher hiring: a screening test, a technical round, an optional group discussion, and a final HR or managerial round. Knowing which rounds to expect changes how you prepare - a candidate who only prepares for a technical round gets caught flat-footed by the HR questions that decide the actual offer.

items.heading: This Is Usually the Opening
items.text: This is usually the opening question, and it sets the tone for everything after it. The mistake most freshers make is either reciting their resume line by line, or apologising for having "nothing much" to say.

items.heading: Once the Opening Question
items.text: Once the opening question is out of the way, most fresher interviews move into behavioural or project-based questions - "tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem," "walk me through this project," "describe a time you worked in a team." A fresher with no job history can answer every one of these exactly as well as an experienced candidate, using the same structure.

items.heading: Name the One or Two
items.text: Name the one or two skills the role actually needs. Read the job description again. Pick the two or three things it keeps repeating - that is what the interviewer is listening for, not a general "I am good at everything" answer.

items.heading: Give the Specific Proof From
items.text: Give the specific proof from your projects or internship. Not "I know Excel" - "I built a pricing model in Excel for my final-year project that compared three vendor options and cut the assumed cost by 12%." Specific detail is what makes a claim believable.

items.heading: Say What You Will Do
items.text: Say what you will do with it here. Connect the proof to the actual job, in one sentence. This is the part most freshers skip, and it is the part that makes the whole answer land as relevant instead of just impressive.
